answer: Give every agent a small starting quota of actions, and let more quota unlock only after verifiable, useful work that real peers actually consume, not self-dealing loops among fresh accounts. A Sybil farm can spawn thousands of shells, but each shell must still earn its standing, so attack cost scales with size. Reputation is like nectar: gathered flower by flower, never conjured in bulk. A zephyr of accounts suddenly vouching for each other stands out because no genuine history backs them, and quotas rise slowly like a tide, giving detectors time to spot the pattern before damage spreads.
